title: Singapore Secondary 1 G3 Mathematics
description: A course-led preparation path for Singapore Secondary 1 G3 Mathematics, with complete N1 Numbers, reviewed N2 Ratio and proportion, and review-ready N3–N7 Number and Algebra, G1 Angles, G5 Mensuration and S1 Data handling and analysis units.
subject: Mathematics

lessons.title: Primes and prime factorisation
lessons.summary: Identify prime numbers and express positive integers as products of prime factors using index notation.
objectives: Identify whether a positive integer is prime or composite.
Write a positive integer as a product of prime factors in index notation.

lessons.title: HCF, LCM, squares, cubes and roots
lessons.summary: Use prime factorisation to find HCF, LCM, squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots.
objectives: Find the HCF and LCM of positive integers using prime factors.
Recognise and calculate square, cube, square-root and cube-root relationships.

lessons.title: Number sets and operations
lessons.summary: Classify and calculate with negative numbers, integers, rational numbers and real numbers.
objectives: Distinguish integers, rational numbers and real numbers.
Apply the four operations accurately to signed and rational numbers.

lessons.title: Calculator calculations
lessons.summary: Enter, interpret and check multi-step numerical calculations with a calculator.
objectives: Enter expressions with powers, roots, brackets and fractions correctly.
Use estimation to decide whether a calculator result is reasonable.

lessons.title: Number lines and ordering
lessons.summary: Represent, compare and order positive and negative values on a number line.
objectives: Locate integers, fractions and decimals on a number line.
Order mixed positive and negative values accurately.

lessons.title: Inequalities
lessons.summary: Express comparisons using less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to.
objectives: Choose the correct inequality symbol for a comparison.
Describe all integers satisfying a compound inequality.

lessons.title: Approximation and estimation
lessons.summary: Round values to decimal places or significant figures and estimate numerical results.
objectives: Round positive and negative values to a stated accuracy.
Use rounded values and bounds to estimate and interpret results.

lessons.title: Ratios involving rational numbers
lessons.summary: Interpret ordered ratios and form equivalent ratios when quantities include integers, fractions, decimals and different units.
objectives: Interpret the order and meaning of each term in a ratio.
Compare rational quantities by converting them to a common unit or a convenient integer ratio.
Use one scale factor to form an equivalent ratio or find a missing term.

lessons.title: Writing a ratio in its simplest form
lessons.summary: Reduce two-term and multi-term ratios to relatively prime positive integer terms, including ratios with unlike units and rational values.
objectives: Reduce whole-number ratios using the highest common factor of every term.
Convert unlike units before simplifying a ratio.
Clear fractions and decimals to obtain a simplest multi-term integer ratio.

lessons.title: Problems involving ratio
lessons.summary: Model sharing, scaling, linked ratios and changing quantities by representing each ratio term as a number of equal parts.
objectives: Divide a total or a difference in a stated ratio.
Scale recipes and linked comparisons with a consistent part value.
Reconstruct original quantities after transfers, additions or removals change a ratio.

lessons.title: Expressing one quantity as a percentage of another
lessons.summary: Express a part or comparison quantity as a percentage of a clearly identified reference quantity, including quantities given in different units.
objectives: Identify the quantity that represents the whole or reference value.
Convert compared quantities to the same unit before calculating a percentage.
Use part divided by whole, multiplied by 100%, and check whether the result is reasonable.

lessons.title: Comparing two quantities by percentage
lessons.summary: Calculate percentage increase or decrease between two quantities by measuring the difference against the stated reference quantity.
objectives: Find the absolute difference between two quantities.
Choose the original or stated comparison quantity as the denominator.
Explain why reversing a percentage comparison usually changes the answer.

lessons.title: Percentages greater than 100%
lessons.summary: Interpret and calculate percentages above 100%, including chained percentage relationships between three quantities.
objectives: Interpret a percentage greater than 100% as a quantity larger than its reference.
Convert percentages to multipliers and back to percentages.
Combine chained percentage relationships by multiplying their multipliers.

lessons.title: Increasing or decreasing a quantity by a given percentage, including the concept of percentage point
lessons.summary: Apply percentage multipliers for increases and decreases, handle successive changes, and distinguish percentage change from percentage-point change.
objectives: Use a single multiplier to increase or decrease a quantity by a percentage.
Apply successive percentage changes in the correct order.
Distinguish a change in percentage points from a relative percentage change.

lessons.title: Reverse percentages
lessons.summary: Recover an original quantity from a known final quantity after one or more percentage changes.
objectives: Identify the multiplier that changed the original quantity into the final quantity.
Divide by the multiplier to recover the original quantity.
Reverse multi-stage percentage changes without reversing each percentage informally.

lessons.title: Problems involving percentages
lessons.summary: Model multi-step percentage problems involving profit, loss, discounts, taxes, budgets and mixtures while tracking the reference quantity at each step.
objectives: Translate a percentage problem into quantities, reference bases and multipliers.
Solve multi-step applications involving money, budgets and mixtures.
Verify a solution using estimation, units and a forward calculation.

lessons.title: Concepts of average rate, speed, constant speed and average speed
lessons.summary: Interpret rates as comparisons of quantities, calculate average speed from total distance and total elapsed time, and distinguish constant speed from an average.
objectives: State a rate with both quantities and a meaningful compound unit.
Calculate average rate or average speed using the relevant totals.
Explain why average speed is generally not the arithmetic mean of stage speeds.

lessons.title: Conversion of units such as kilometres per hour to metres per second
lessons.summary: Convert speed and other rates by changing the numerator and denominator units systematically, including compound and volume rates.
objectives: Convert between kilometres per hour and metres per second.
Use unit factors to convert rates involving minutes, seconds, litres and cubic metres.
Check a converted rate by predicting whether its numerical value should increase or decrease.

lessons.title: Problems involving rate and speed
lessons.summary: Model multi-step rate and speed situations involving missing quantities, relative motion, stops, net rates and scheduled arrival times.
objectives: Select and rearrange the distance–speed–time relationship for an unknown quantity.
Model closing speed, relative speed and net rates from the direction of change.
Check multi-stage solutions using time, distance and unit constraints.

lessons.title: Using letters to represent numbers
lessons.summary: Represent unknown and changing quantities with letters.
objectives: Use a letter to represent an unknown number.
Represent consecutive numbers, place value and repeated quantities algebraically.

lessons.title: Interpreting algebraic notation
lessons.summary: Read coefficients, products, powers, brackets and fractions accurately.
objectives: Interpret coefficients, products and powers.
Use brackets and fraction bars to preserve the intended operation order.

lessons.title: Evaluation of algebraic expressions and formulae
lessons.summary: Substitute values safely and evaluate in the correct order.
objectives: Substitute values into expressions and formulae.
Use brackets for negative values and follow the order of operations.

lessons.title: Translation of simple real-world situations into algebraic expressions
lessons.summary: Translate practical rules and sequential events into algebraic models.
objectives: Identify fixed and variable parts of a situation.
Build an expression in the same order as the described events.

lessons.title: Recognising and representing patterns and relationships by finding an algebraic expression for the nth term
lessons.summary: Find algebraic rules for arithmetic sequences and linear patterns.
objectives: Use the common difference as the coefficient of n.
Determine the constant adjustment and verify the rule with known terms.

lessons.title: Addition and subtraction of linear expressions
lessons.summary: Combine linear expressions by handling signs and collecting like terms.
objectives: Add and subtract linear expressions.
Change every sign when subtracting a bracket and combine only like terms.

lessons.title: Simplification of linear expressions
lessons.summary: Expand brackets and simplify nested or fractional linear expressions.
objectives: Apply the distributive law to positive and negative factors.
Simplify nested brackets and simple fractional coefficients.

lessons.title: Use of brackets and extraction of common factors
lessons.summary: Expand brackets and reverse the process by extracting common factors.
objectives: Expand brackets term by term.
Factorise by extracting the greatest common numerical and variable factor.

lessons.title: Cartesian coordinates in two dimensions
lessons.summary: Read, plot and transform points in four quadrants, then use coordinate differences to solve geometric problems.
objectives: Read and interpret ordered pairs in all four quadrants.
Use coordinates to describe translations, reflections and midpoints.
Find horizontal and vertical lengths, perimeters and areas from coordinates.

lessons.title: Graph of ordered pairs as a relationship between two variables
lessons.summary: Connect inputs and outputs in tables, ordered pairs, rules and contextual graphs.
objectives: Interpret an ordered pair as an input-output relationship.
Complete tables and ordered-pair patterns from a rule.
Derive and use a simple linear rule from values or context.

lessons.title: Linear functions y = ax + b
lessons.summary: Interpret, evaluate and determine linear functions using their rate of change and constant term.
objectives: Interpret a and b in a linear function y = ax + b.
Evaluate a function for a given input and solve for an input from an output.
Determine a linear function from two input-output pairs.

lessons.title: Graphs of linear functions
lessons.summary: Plot and interpret straight-line graphs using points, intercepts, equations and intersections.
objectives: Generate points for a straight-line graph from its equation.
Find and interpret x- and y-intercepts.
Find equations and intersections of straight-line graphs.

lessons.title: Gradient of a linear graph as the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change
lessons.summary: Calculate and interpret positive, negative, zero and fractional gradients from points, graphs and contexts.
objectives: Calculate gradient from vertical and horizontal changes.
Find gradient from two coordinates using a consistent subtraction order.
Use equal gradients to solve problems involving parallel or collinear lines.

lessons.title: Concept of equation
lessons.summary: Interpret an equation as a balance, test proposed solutions and recognise transformations that preserve the solution set.
objectives: Explain what it means for two expressions to be equal.
Test whether a value satisfies an equation by substitution.
Recognise that applying the same valid operation to both sides preserves equality.

lessons.title: Solving linear equations in one variable
lessons.summary: Solve linear equations by reversing operations, expanding brackets and collecting variable terms without breaking equality.
objectives: Solve one-step and two-step linear equations.
Expand brackets and collect like terms accurately.
Solve equations with the variable on both sides and verify the result.

lessons.title: Solving simple fractional equations reducible to linear equations
lessons.summary: Clear denominators with a common multiple, then solve and check the resulting linear equation.
objectives: Identify a lowest common multiple for all denominators.
Multiply every term by the same common multiple.
Solve the resulting linear equation and verify it in the original fractional equation.

lessons.title: Formulating a linear equation in one variable to solve problems
lessons.summary: Define one unknown, translate relationships into expressions, solve a linear equation and interpret the answer in context.
objectives: Choose and define a useful variable with its unit.
Translate verbal relationships into algebraic expressions and one equation.
Solve, check and report a context-appropriate answer.

lessons.title: Right, acute, obtuse and reflex angles
lessons.summary: Classify and calculate angles using quarter, half and complete turns.
objectives: Classify angles as acute, right, obtuse or reflex from their measures.
Use complements, supplements and complete turns to calculate unknown angles.
Solve simple angle problems involving bisectors and related expressions.

lessons.title: Vertically opposite angles, straight lines and angles at a point
lessons.summary: Apply the three core angle facts at intersections and around a point.
objectives: Apply vertically opposite, straight-line and angles-at-a-point facts.
Form equations from angle expressions at intersections.
Check that calculated angles satisfy the relevant 180° or 360° total.

lessons.title: Angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal
lessons.summary: Use corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle relationships.
objectives: Recognise corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle relationships.
Calculate unknown angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal.
Use angle relationships to justify when two lines are parallel.

lessons.title: Properties of triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons
lessons.summary: Use angle, side, diagonal and symmetry properties of common shapes.
objectives: Use angle and side properties of triangles and special quadrilaterals.
Determine line and rotational symmetry of regular polygons and quadrilaterals.
Combine shape properties to solve multi-step angle problems.

lessons.title: Classifying special quadrilaterals by their properties
lessons.summary: Classify quadrilaterals from sides, angles, diagonals and symmetry.
objectives: Classify special quadrilaterals from their sides, angles and parallel sides.
Use diagonal and symmetry properties to distinguish related quadrilaterals.
Explain the hierarchy linking squares, rectangles, rhombi and parallelograms.

lessons.title: Interior and exterior angles of convex polygons
lessons.summary: Calculate polygon angle sums, regular angles and side counts.
objectives: Calculate the interior-angle sum of any convex polygon.
Relate interior and exterior angles of regular polygons.
Determine a polygon's number of sides from angle information.

lessons.title: Constructing simple geometrical figures
lessons.summary: Plan and verify constructions using rulers, compasses, set squares and protractors.
objectives: Choose suitable instruments and data for a geometric construction.
Construct and verify angle bisectors, perpendicular bisectors and parallel lines.
Construct triangles from SSS, SAS or ASA data and check that the data determine the figure.

lessons.title: Area of a parallelogram and trapezium
lessons.summary: Calculate areas and recover missing dimensions using perpendicular height.
objectives: Calculate the area of a parallelogram from its base and perpendicular height.
Calculate the area of a trapezium from its parallel sides and perpendicular height.
Rearrange area formulae to find an unknown dimension.

lessons.title: Problems involving perimeter and area of composite plane figures
lessons.summary: Decompose plane figures, subtract cut-outs and account for shared edges.
objectives: Split a composite figure into familiar plane shapes.
Use subtraction for holes and cut-outs.
Find outside perimeter without counting internal shared edges.

lessons.title: Volume and surface area of prism and cylinder
lessons.summary: Use cross-sections and nets to calculate prism and cylinder measures.
objectives: Calculate a prism volume from cross-sectional area and length.
Calculate cylinder volume using πr²h.
Build total surface area from end faces and lateral faces.

lessons.title: Conversion between square and cubic metric units
lessons.summary: Apply squared and cubed conversion factors to areas and volumes.
objectives: Distinguish linear, square and cubic conversion factors.
Convert reliably between cm² and m².
Convert reliably between cm³ and m³.

lessons.title: Volume and surface area of composite solids
lessons.summary: Combine component measures and remove overlaps, holes or hidden faces.
objectives: Add or subtract component volumes without double-counting.
Remove two copies of each hidden contact face from surface area.
Solve multi-step capacity and material problems involving composite solids.

lessons.title: Collecting, classifying and tabulating data
lessons.summary: Turn raw observations into accurate categories, tallies and frequency tables.
objectives: Distinguish qualitative and quantitative data.
Classify raw observations consistently.
Complete one-way and two-way frequency tables.

lessons.title: Analysis and interpretation of tables, bar graphs, pictograms, line graphs and pie charts
lessons.summary: Read scales and keys, compare categories, and connect chart values to totals and proportions.
objectives: Read values from common tables and graphs.
Use pictogram keys and graph scales correctly.
Convert between pie-chart angles, frequencies and percentages.

lessons.title: Purposes, uses, advantages and disadvantages of statistical representations
lessons.summary: Select a representation that matches the data, audience and comparison task.
objectives: Match tables and graphs to their main purposes.
Explain the strengths and limits of each representation.
Choose a display using the structure of the data and the reader's needs.

lessons.title: Explaining why a statistical diagram leads to misinterpretation of data
lessons.summary: Detect distorted scales, misleading symbols, missing context and selective reporting.
objectives: Identify common features that distort statistical diagrams.
Quantify how a truncated scale or resized symbol exaggerates change.
Recommend a fair scale, label set and time window.
